title: Rethinking Empathy in the Age of AI: Human–Machine Collaboration and the Future of Emotional Intelligence
summary: Artificial intelligence is transforming empathy into a strategic capability. Discover how collaboration between humans and machines will redefine leadership, the customer experience and emotional intelligence
body_text: Human–Machine Coexistence: Why We Need to Rethink Empathy We are continuously monitoring our internal trend radar, where we define overarching developments and trends that directly impact and shape our organization. One of these trends is human–machine coexistence , which raises fundamental questions about empathy, responsibility, and collaboration in the age of AI: What if we need to rethink empathy? What if machines are better at simulating empathy? What if machines could help us understand both other humans and machines better? And: What if we outsource empathy to machines? Artificial intelligence is rapidly moving beyond pure automation. Its potential lies not only in performing tasks faster or more efficiently, but in enhancing activities once considered uniquely human, such as moral judgment, care, or empathic communication . From Automation to Emotional Intelligence: Changing Customer Expectations This trend is already reflected in evolving customer expectations . When interacting with machines, users no longer expect only speed—they expect fairness, respect, and meaningful engagement. AI is no longer judged solely by its accuracy or technical performance, but by how it makes people feel . As expectations rise, so does the pressure on organizations to deliver not just seamless experiences, but emotionally resonant ones—at scale. AI and Empathy: Why Machines Are Perceived as More Empathic Empathy is now at the center of human–machine collaboration . AI systems can simulate empathic responses with remarkable convincingness. In many contexts, they are rated as more empathic than humans—precisely because they are consistent, attentive, and free from fatigue or emotional volatility. Various studies found that AI-generated messages can make recipients feel more heard than human-generated ones and are often better at detecting emotions. However, once recipients realized that a message came from AI rather than a human, the perceived empathic impact declined. The Real Advantage: Orchestrating Human and AI Empathy While machines may express empathy linguistically, human presence remains psychologically important . The competitive advantage does not lie in choosing between AI empathy and human empathy, but in orchestrating both : designing systems in which AI enhances empathic quality, while humans provide authenticity, relational depth, and ethical grounding. This orchestration opens up powerful opportunities. Leaders can leverage AI-generated insights to communicate with greater clarity, empathy, and consistency. Emotion-aware systems can enrich interactions, increase engagement, and provide support across long, high-volume processes without exhaustion. Risks of AI-Driven Empathy: Manipulation and Echo Chambers These developments also carry significant risks. Simulated empathy can mask misaligned intentions, creating systems that appear caring while manipulating users or optimizing for non-human goals. Another danger lies in the creation of echo chambers , where sophisticated empathy mechanisms reinforce existing beliefs instead of challenging them—potentially amplifying distorted perceptions or, in vulnerable users, contributing to harmful psychological dynamics. This risk transforms empathy from a mechanism of understanding into a mechanism of validation. What Comes Next: AI, Robotics, and the Future of Human-Like Expression The next milestone is already emerging. A research team led by Professor Hod Lipson at Columbia University has developed a new generation of robotics capable of highly precise, real-time facial synchronization with speech—a major step toward human-like expressiveness. As Lipson states: “I guarantee you in a few years they are going to look like humans.” This raises a critical question: What happens when machines not only simulate empathetic language, but also surpass humans in facial emotional expression ? Empathy as a Strategic Capability in the Age of AI Empathy is no longer a purely human trait. It is becoming a strategic capability for organizations , one that must be deliberately designed and governed. The future belongs to organizations that understand empathy as a capability built at the intersection of humans and machines , combining technological scalability with human authenticity. Telefónica Value Proposition: Driving Responsible AI with Strategic Impact In this context, Telefónica embraces the challenge of becoming the leading gateway for citizens to access digital technologies, driving a transformation built on five key pillars: strengthening its European leadership by contributing to technological sovereignty; building a more innovative and competitive organization through simplification, efficiency, and highly skilled talent; delivering superior customer services supported by best-in-class networks and trust; advancing with ambitious, disciplined, and results-driven management; and reinforcing its role as a key institutional reference for Spain in Europe. Ultimately, the goal is to transform artificial intelligence into a responsible, human-centered capability that creates sustainable value for businesses, customers, and society.

title: Flowspace Launches Fulfillment Freedom Fund, Providing Up to $50,000 in Transition Support to Help Brands Switch from Restrictive 3PL Providers
summary: Flowspace's Fulfillment Freedom Fund offers up to $50,000 to help brands switch from restrictive 3PL providers. Applications close September 30, 2026.
body_text: A first-of-its-kind transition support program helps ecommerce brands overcome the financial barriers of changing 3PL providers, accelerating cost savings and long-term growth. LOS ANGELES--( BUSINESS WIRE )--Flowspace, a modern fulfillment provider that combines powerful technology with expert fulfillment operations, today announced the launch of the Flowspace Fulfillment Freedom Fund , a first-of-its-kind transition support program designed to help ecommerce brands transition from restrictive and outdated third-party logistics (3PL) providers and unlock a more flexible, cost-effective fulfillment strategy. For many growing brands, the decision to leave a bad 3PL is obvious — but the cost of making the switch is not. Contract termination fees, inventory transfers, system integrations, and implementation costs often prevent businesses from leaving underperforming 3PLs, even when those providers actively drive up costs, provide limited visibility, and lack flexibility to support their growth. The Flowspace Fulfillment Freedom Fund removes those barriers by providing eligible businesses with an order volume-based transition fund of up to $50,000 , helping offset the costs associated with switching fulfillment providers and accelerating time to value. "Too many brands know their fulfillment partner isn't delivering the service, flexibility, or cost savings they need, but the expense of making a change keeps them stuck," said Ben Eachus, CEO and Co-founder of Flowspace. "We created the Fulfillment Freedom Fund, a first-of-its-kind program to remove that obstacle. Brands should choose the fulfillment partner that's best for their business, not the one they're financially locked into." Flowspace pairs coast-to-coast fulfillment centers with an AI-supported platform that gives brands a single system of record for inventory, orders, and fulfillment performance — the kind of visibility that legacy 3PLs often can't provide. The result: distributed inventory placed where demand actually is, shipping rates optimized in real time, and order routing that gets packages moving faster, all backed by a fulfillment team focused on one thing: growth. Flowspace customers save up to 20% on shipping costs, and one high-volume brand saved over $1 million annually , thanks to exclusive optimized shipping rates, inventory placement, and operational efficiencies. The Fulfillment Freedom Fund helps brands begin realizing those savings sooner by offsetting the costs of switching providers. Eligible businesses may receive: Up to $50,000 in order volume-based transition support to offset 3PL contract exit fees, implementation costs, inventory transfers, and other switching expenses Dedicated onboarding and implementation resources Access to Flowspace's U.S. and Canada fulfillment locations, technology platform, and fulfillment expertise The program reflects Flowspace's commitment to helping brands build more resilient and cost-effective fulfillment operations as rising shipping costs and increasing customer expectations continue to pressure margins. Unlike long-term 3PL contracts that lock brands into inflexible operations, Flowspace is investing in customer success by removing one of the biggest barriers to a better, long-term fulfillment decision. "Our customers consistently tell us they wish they'd switched 3PLs sooner," added Eachus. "This program is about giving brands the confidence to move forward by removing one of the biggest obstacles to choosing a fulfillment partner that's built to help them grow ." Applications for the current program are open until September 30, 2026 , to a select number of businesses. Eligibility is based on monthly order volume, sales channels, and vertical, and is granted at Flowspace's sole discretion. Accepted brands agree to a 15-month partnership with Flowspace. For more information about joining the current program for the Flowspace Fulfillment Freedom Fund or to determine eligibility, visit flow.space/fund or schedule a consultation with a Flowspace fulfillment expert. Terms and conditions apply. About Flowspace Flowspace is a modern fulfillment provider that combines powerful technology with expert fulfillment operations to deliver seamless and scalable execution that moves with your business. Through its nationwide fulfillment centers, automated, AI-supported software, and experienced operations teams, Flowspace helps brands optimize inventory, reduce shipping costs, improve delivery performance, and scale with confidence. ‍

title: Protect Yourself From Fake Login and Verification Code Requests
summary: Cybercriminals use deceptive methods to trick individuals into approving unauthorized account access or sharing verification codes, so it is essential to stay vigilant and protect your accounts.
body_text: News Details Friday, July 17, 2026 Cybercriminals use convincing emails, text messages, phone calls, and pop-ups to trick people into approving account access or sharing verification codes. Some scams may even send you to a real sign-in or verification page, but that does not mean the request is safe if you did not start it. How to Protect Yourself Never approve a login request you did not start Never enter or share a verification code because someone emailed, texted, or called and asked you to do so Be cautious of unexpected messages asking you to open a shared document, review a voicemail, view an invoice, verify your account, enter a code, or approve access Take a moment to review any login or authorization request before approving it Go directly to a trusted website or app instead of using links in unexpected messages Use strong passwords and enable multifactor authentication whenever available Remember: multifactor authentication is an important layer of protection, but only approve prompts or enter codes for sign-ins you personally started Always confirm you are at firstmerchants.com or on the FMB Banking app before you log in—do not follow links from search results or ads without checking the URL Remember First Merchants will never contact you and pressure you to share a password, provide a verification code, or approve a login request you did not initiate. Be especially cautious of requests involving login approvals, verification codes, or account validation. If something seems unusual, pause and confirm before proceeding. Staying vigilant is one of the best ways to protect yourself from online fraud and account compromise. If You Receive a Suspicious Request Do not respond, do not enter the code, and do not approve the request. If you believe you may have interacted with a scam, contact your local First Merchants branch or Customer Care at 1.800.205.3464 .

title: Cloud-Based ATS: How the Technology Works and Why Startups Adopt It (June 2026)
summary: Cloud-based ATS software runs remotely with no IT overhead. Compare free and paid options, AI features, and setup time for startups in June 2026.
body_text: Employers across industries rely on a mix of well-known systems, and understanding which names appear most often helps job seekers and hiring teams alike assess the market. The most frequently encountered cloud-based ATS tools include Workday, Greenhouse, Lever, iCIMS, Taleo (Oracle), Jobvite, BambooHR, Rippling, and Ashby. Larger enterprises tend to gravitate toward Workday and Taleo, while growth-stage startups more commonly use Greenhouse, Lever, or Ashby. How These Systems Differ in Practice The names on any list of ATS systems can look interchangeable, but the products vary considerably in scope and target buyer. Workday is an enterprise HR suite where the ATS is one module inside a much larger system. It carries a steep configuration cost and is typically managed by a dedicated HR ops team, which makes it rare for companies below a few hundred employees. Greenhouse is widely used at mid-size tech companies. It offers structured hiring workflows and strong integration support, though its pricing scales up quickly as headcount grows. Lever combines ATS functionality with candidate relationship management, which means recruiters can track passive candidates alongside active applicants in a single view. Ashby has gained traction with technical startups for its reporting depth and cleaner interface, often appearing in hiring discussions on forums where recruiters compare tools. BambooHR and Rippling package applicant tracking inside broader HR software, making them appealing when a small team wants to consolidate HR administration and recruiting into one system. iCIMS and Jobvite sit closer to the enterprise end, with configurable workflows suited to high-volume recruiting operations.

title: SmartRent's Wyron Bobis leads the connectivity discussion at Apartmentalize '24
summary: Highlights from Apartmentalize ’24 connectivity discussion—insights on network design, IoT integrations resident apps and strategies to future‑proof multifamily tech.
body_text: Subscribe to our newsletter Community connectivity took center stage at NAA Apartmentalize 2024 in Philadelphia, where thousands of professionals gathered. SmartRent Executive Vice President of Operations Wyron Bobis moderated an express education session titled “Seamless Connectivity: Where in the WiFi is Waldo?” joined by panelists Jennifer Kent of Parks Associates and Ivy Christman of Quest Management Group. Unlike fans of the classic “Where’s Waldo?” picture search puzzles, rental housing operators and residents shouldn’t have to hunt for a WiFi signal in their communities. Yet, the reality is stark: while Waldo roams freely across jumbled pages, only 1% of apartment residents can seamlessly roam their communities on private access points without losing connectivity. This gap presents a significant opportunity for multifamily operators to enhance resident satisfaction and operational efficiency. Multifamily communities are upgrading their WiFi systems, moving away from choice internet (where residents source their own provider) and legacy or “bulk” WiFi obtained at a discount by management companies. Community WiFi, a more advanced solution, offers community-wide connectivity through in-home and shared access points. “WiFi is one of those things that’s ubiquitous and behind the scenes, but there’s a lot of nuances about how it’s provided,” said Jennifer Kent, Vice President of Research at Parks Associates. “Residents feel the pain of poor deployments.” Kent shared a Parks Associates study on the correlation between WiFi service and renter satisfaction. The survey asked for a net promoter score (NPS) — a measure of customer loyalty ranging from -100 to 100 — for both properties and internet service. The study revealed striking differences: Residents with choice/retail internet in their communities scored their WiFi service at a 7.1 NPS while giving their properties an abysmal -20.2. Residents in communities with legacy/bulk WiFi scored their communities even worse, with identical -27.5 NPS ratings for both their properties and WiFi service. Residents living in communities with managed WiFi submitted promoter scores of 6.4 for their properties and an impressive 19.1 for their WiFi. These scores clearly demonstrate the positive impact of community WiFi on resident satisfaction . “Younger renters want connectivity at the pool and other amenities. Anything that’s more seamless and more viable for their daily lives is appreciated,” Christman said. “We want to be proactive. Community-wide WiFi is part of our three-year plan at all our properties.” While new developments are an ideal time to deploy community WiFi, Bobis said the benefits have many management companies tackling retrofit projects. “Retrofit is definitely more complicated than new development, but the end result is worth the work,” Bobis said. “There are a lot of resident considerations when you install the new infrastructure. When you pull new cable, you have to cut access holes. Sometimes you have to go below ground and find a new path to route cables. Project management is a huge key because there are a lot of moving parts.” Retrofits average between four and seven months, Bobis said, depending on the fiber connection setup schedule. “When all is said and done, you have to make sure you have the least disruption to current residents,” Bobis said. “Then, after installation, a lot of testing needs to be done to make sure you have a strong signal throughout the property.” The demand for strong, consistent WiFi is undeniable. “What surprised me is the number of devices people have connected to WiFi. I guess you just don’t think about it,” said Bobis. “Data shows an average of seven connected devices, and people are spending an average of 60 hours a week online.” Community WiFi benefits extend beyond residents. Community management teams need access to property management systems and other technologies. “It’s not just about individual access,” Kent added. “Community WiFi is the backbone that allows IoT devices to come online.” Community WiFi enables owners and operators to connect smart devices such as thermostats, lighting, plug-ins, window shades, leak detectors and humidity sensors under a single dashboard, amplifying their collective impact. IoT networks enhance asset efficiency, risk mitigation, and energy savings and directly contribute to NOI. Operators can also create ancillary income by passing through WiFi fees to residents. A Parks Associates survey showed an increasing willingness to pay for modern WiFi, with 64% of renters willing to pay $49.99 for 300 Mbps speeds and 35% willing to pay $99.99 for 2+ Gbps speeds. Christman noted that residents generally prefer bundled fees with rent or amenities for simpler budgeting. Meeting evolving renter demands As the multifamily industry evolves, community WiFi emerges as a powerful solution to meet resident expectations and streamline operations. By investing in robust, property-wide connectivity, owners and operators can boost satisfaction scores, enable smart home technologies, and potentially create new revenue streams. In today’s connected world, seamless WiFi is no longer a luxury—it’s an essential amenity that can set properties apart in a competitive market.
